items.title: Panicked Sam Altman Reverses Position as Walls Close In, Says People Should Be Able to Own RAM
items.summary:
During a recent podcast appearance, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman made some baffling comments that really hit a nerve on social media. The billionaire said that it didn’t make sense for individual people to run their own AI models at home and that all of their RAM chips were far better off being used inside the industry’s widely-reviled data centers. [...] The flap illustrates wildly diverging conceptions of AI. To the people leading the industry, it’s a technological revolution. To the disillusioned public — and especially furious PC enthusiasts — it’s an enormous waste of resources that could backfire in spectacular fashion as strained financial markets reach a breaking point.

More on Altman: Sam Altman Absolutely Hates the Idea of People Running Their Own AI Models at Home, Argues They Shouldn’t Own Computers [...] Futurism Logo

# Panicked Sam Altman Reverses Position as Walls Close In, Says People Should Be Able to Own RAM

"I want you to have so much ram."

By Victor Tangermann

Published

Getty Images / Shutterstock / Futurism

items.title: Sam Altman thinks it's 'quite terrible' for your PC to be using memory that AI companies need so badly
items.summary:
Among the many impacts the AI industry has had on the world in the last several years, the ongoing memory shortage is one of the biggest. OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and other tech giants are gobbling up the world's memory supply to power their data centers, sending prices for consumer electronics skyrocketing. Given that context, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman thinks it's "quite terrible" that you have memory sitting in your computer that AI companies could be using instead. [...] Altman's comments have not gone over well online. "He sees anyone owning something for their own personal use as a resource that he's being denied," one Reddit user said on the website's r/Technology board. "Sam Altman is [mad] at resources being used by other people for their own use instead of being used to make him richer," another added. That sentiment carried through most of the comments throughout the thread.

Advertisement

Advertisement [...] Altman's comments came in a recent interview with Stripe cofounder John Collison, where he discussed the surge in interest in running open-source AI models on local hardware (like your own PC) rather than relying on big AI companies to handle the processing in the cloud. "From, like, a global allocation perspective, actually it's quite terrible to have everybody, like, have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their computer and being used 5% of the time," Altman said.

items.title: OpenAI's Sam Altman Backtracks After Hating on You for Having RAM - CNET
items.summary: What does Sam Altman, CEO of ChatGPT creator OpenAI, think about you using RAM (aka memory) in the computer you own? It’s tough to say, because he’s made multiple contradictory statements following an interview last week where he said, “It’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer.”

items.title: Sam Altman Backtracked on His Most Absurd AI Claim Yet. Sort of
items.summary:
Last week, on a podcast, Sam Altman suggested that your computer is a terribly inefficient use of RAM and that AI companies should have it instead. Or, at least, that’s definitely what it seemed like he was saying.

Now, he wants you to know that he was taken out of context and, actually, he thinks you should have as much RAM as you want. In fact, he thinks you should have more RAM than you know what to do with. Maybe?
